To proceed: this is the eighty-fifth of the weekly sessions, which take place every Thursday. This Thursday is the eleventh of the month of Sha'ban in the year one thousand four hundred and fifteen (AH). As usual, we begin by explaining what we reached in the thirtieth part of the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. We have reached Surah al-Qadr, where Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree. And what can make you know what the Night of Decree is? The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months﴾ [al-Qadr 1-3].

Allah mentioned Himself in the plural of majesty, ﴿Indeed, We sent it down﴾, rather than saying "Indeed, I sent it down," because He, Glorified and Exalted, is the Great, and nothing is greater than Him.

And We have enumerated all things in a clear register﴾ [Ya-Sin 12]. Sometimes He refers to Himself in the singular, as in: ﴿Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance﴾ [Ta-Ha 14]. This is because He is one who is great. The plural of majesty comes in regard to His attributes, and the singular comes in regard to His oneness.

The pronoun in His saying ﴿We sent it down﴾, namely the object pronoun "hu," refers to the Qur'an even though it has not been mentioned before, because this is a known matter, and no one doubts that what is meant is the sending down of the Noble Qur'an, which Allah sent down during the Night of Decree. So what is the meaning of its being sent down during the Night of Decree?

The correct view is that its meaning is: We began sending it down during the Night of Decree. The Night of Decree is in Ramadan, without any doubt. The evidence for this is His saying: ﴿The month of Ramadan is that in which the Qur'an was revealed as guidance for the people and as clear proofs of guidance and criterion﴾ [al-Baqarah 185]. When you combine this verse, namely ﴿the month of Ramadan is that in which the Qur'an was revealed﴾, with the verse we are discussing, it becomes clear to you that the Night of Decree is in Ramadan. From this we know that what is widespread among the common people, that the Night of Decree is the night of the middle of Sha'ban, has no basis and no reality, since the Night of Decree is in Ramadan.

The night of the middle of Sha'ban is like the night of the middle of Rajab, Jumada, Rabi', Safar, Muharram, and other months. It is not specific to anything. As for what has been narrated concerning the virtue of standing in prayer on that night, these are weak hadiths that cannot establish proof. Likewise, what has been narrated concerning singling out its day, which is the fifteenth of Sha'ban, for fasting, these are weak hadiths that cannot establish proof. However, some scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, are lenient in mentioning weak hadiths concerning virtues, whether the virtues of deeds, months, or places. This is not appropriate, because when you narrate weak hadiths about the virtue of anything, the listener will believe it to be authentic and attribute it to the Messenger, peace be upon him, and this is a serious matter. The important point is that the day of the middle of Sha'ban and the night of the middle of Sha'ban are not specific to anything over the rest of the months. The night of the middle is not specific to a virtue of standing in prayer, the night of the middle is not the Night of Decree, and the day of the middle is not specific to fasting.

Yes, regarding the month of Sha'ban, the Sunnah has established that the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, would fast much during it, so that he broke his fast in it only rarely. As for everything else related to his fasting in it, nothing has been established from the Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, except what applies to the other months, such as the virtue of fasting three days of every month, and that these be on the thirteenth, fourteenth, and fifteenth, which are the "White Days" (al-Ayyam al-Bid).

As for His saying ﴿during the Night of Decree﴾, what is the meaning of ﴿Decree﴾? Is it honour, as one says, "So-and-so has great standing" or "great standing," meaning great honour? Or is the meaning of ﴿Decree﴾ the determining, because in it is determined what will occur during the year, as Allah says: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Indeed, We were ever warning. In it is made distinct every precise matter﴾ [ad-Dukhan 3-4], meaning: it is separated and made clear?

Among the scholars are those who said this, and those who said that. The correct view is that it encompasses both meanings. The Night of Decree is without doubt of great standing and great honour, and in it is determined what will occur in that year of giving life and causing death, of provisions, and other matters.

Then He, Mighty and Exalted, said: ﴿And what can make you know what the Night of Decree is?﴾ This sentence in this form indicates glorification and exaltation, and it recurs in the Noble Qur'an. Allah says: ﴿And what can make you know what the Day of Judgement is? Then what can make you know what the Day of Judgement is?﴾ [al-Infitar 17-18], and He says: ﴿The Inevitable Reality. What is the Inevitable Reality?﴾ [al-Haqqah 1-2], and ﴿The Striking Calamity. What is the Striking Calamity? And what can make you know what the Striking Calamity is?﴾ [al-Qari'ah 1-3]. Then He mentioned what happens in that night, saying: ﴿The angels and the Spirit descend therein﴾ [al-Qadr 4]. ﴿Descend﴾ means they descend little by little, because the angels are the inhabitants of the heavens, and the heavens are seven. So the angels descend to the earth gradually until they fill the earth. The descent of the angels to the earth is a sign of mercy, goodness, and blessing. For this reason, when the angels refrain from entering something, that is evidence that this place which the angels refrain from entering may be devoid of goodness and blessing, such as a place in which there are pictures. The Prophet said: "Indeed, the angels do not enter a house in which there is a picture" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (5958) and Muslim (2106/85) from the hadith of Abu Talhah al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him]. This means a forbidden picture, because if the picture is used as a cushion or a pillow, most scholars hold it to be permissible. Accordingly, the angels do not refrain from entering the place, because if they did refrain, that would be prohibited. The angels descend in great numbers during the Night of Decree, and their descent is good and blessing.

His saying ﴿by permission of their Lord﴾ [al-Qadr 4] means: by His command. What is meant is the universal permission (al-idhn al-kawni, meaning permission through divine decree), because the permission of Allah, that is, His command, is divided into two kinds: universal permission and legislative permission (al-idhn al-shar'i). Allah described it as peace because of the large number of people who are kept safe in it from sins and their punishments. The Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, said: "Whoever stands in prayer during the Night of Decree out of faith and seeking reward, his previous sins will be forgiven" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1901) and Muslim (760/175) from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him]. The forgiveness of sins is without doubt a safety from their harm and punishments.

﴿Until the emergence of dawn﴾ [al-Qadr 5], meaning: the angels descend during this night until the emergence of dawn. When dawn breaks, the Night of Decree ends.

We have said before that the Night of Decree is in Ramadan without doubt, but in which part of Ramadan: is it at its beginning, its middle, or its end?

In answering this, we say: "The Prophet ﷺ performed i'tikaf (seclusion in the mosque) during the first ten days, then during the middle ten days, seeking the Night of Decree. Then he was told that it is in the last ten days, so he performed i'tikaf during the last ten days" [al-Bukhari, whose wording this is (813), and Muslim (1167/215), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ performed i'tikaf during the first ten days of Ramadan, and we performed i'tikaf with him. Then Gabriel came to him and said: 'What you seek is ahead of you.' So he performed i'tikaf during the middle ten days, and we performed i'tikaf with him. Then Gabriel came to him and said: 'What you seek is ahead of you.' The Prophet ﷺ stood to deliver a sermon on the morning of the twentieth of Ramadan and said: 'Whoever has performed i'tikaf with the Prophet ﷺ, let him return, for I was shown the Night of Decree, but I was made to forget it, and it is in the last ten days, in an odd night. I saw myself prostrating in mud and water.'"]. Therefore, it, namely the Night of Decree, is in the last ten days of Ramadan.

Which night of them? Allah knows best. It may be the night of the twenty-first, or the night of the thirtieth, or what lies between them. No specific night has been fixed each year. For this reason, "the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, was shown the Night of Decree, the night of the twenty-first, and he saw in a dream that he was prostrating in the morning of it in water and mud. The sky rained that night, that is, the night of the twenty-first, and the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, prayed in his mosque, which was made of palm-leaf thatch that did not prevent water from seeping through the roof. So the Prophet ﷺ prostrated in the morning, that is, in the dawn prayer, in water and mud, and the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, saw on his forehead the traces of water and mud." In that year it was on the night of the twenty-first. Nevertheless he said: "Seek it in the last ten days" [al-Bukhari, whose wording this is (2027), and Muslim (1167/213), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to perform i'tikaf in the middle ten days of Ramadan, and he performed i'tikaf for a year, until when it was the night of the twenty-first, the night from whose morning he would leave his i'tikaf, he said: "Whoever has performed i'tikaf with me, let him perform i'tikaf in the last ten days. I was shown this night and then made to forget it, and I saw myself prostrating in water and mud from its morning. So seek it in the last ten days, and seek it in every odd night." The sky rained that night, and the mosque was made of palm-leaf thatch, so the mosque leaked, and my eyes saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with the traces of water and mud on his forehead from the morning of the twenty-first.] And in another narration: "In the odd nights of the last ten" [al-Bukhari (2017) from the hadith of Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her].

The Companions saw it in one year of the years in the last seven nights. The Prophet ﷺ said: "I see that your visions agree on the last seven nights, so whoever seeks it, let him seek it in the last seven nights" [agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2015) and Muslim (1165), from the hadith of Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both]. This means in that year. As for the other years, it may be in any of the last ten nights, and it is not fixed to a particular one. But the night it is most hoped to be is the twenty-seventh night. It is most likely to be the twenty-seventh night. For example, it may be the twenty-seventh night in this year, the twenty-first night in the second year, the twenty-fifth night in the third year, and so on.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, concealed it for two great benefits:

The first benefit: to show who is sincere in seeking it from the lazy. The one who is sincere in seeking it does not mind exerting himself for ten nights in order to attain it, whereas the lazy person may become lax, saying: since I do not know which night it is, he is lazy about standing in prayer for ten nights for the sake of one night.

The second benefit: to multiply the reward of the Muslims through the multiplication of deeds, because the more the deeds, the greater the reward.

On this occasion, I would like to point out the error of many people nowadays, who seek the twenty-seventh night for performing 'umrah (the minor pilgrimage). On the twenty-seventh night you find the Sacred Mosque filled with people in large numbers. Singling out the twenty-seventh night for 'umrah is a bid'ah (religious innovation), because the Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, did not single it out for 'umrah in his actions, nor did he single it out, that is, the twenty-seventh night, for 'umrah in his words. He did not perform 'umrah on the twenty-seventh night of Ramadan, even though in the year of the Conquest he was in Makkah on the twenty-seventh night of Ramadan, and he did not perform 'umrah, nor did he tell the Ummah: seek the twenty-seventh night for 'umrah. Rather, he commanded us to seek the twenty-seventh night for standing in prayer during it, not for 'umrah. By this, the error of many people becomes clear. By this also it becomes clear that people may take their religion from one elder to another without any foundation in the Shari'ah. So beware of worshipping Allah except with insight, based on evidence from the Book of Allah, the Sunnah of His Messenger, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, or the practice of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, whose Sunnah we have been commanded to follow.

With this, the discussion of Surah al-Qadr is concluded. We ask Allah, Blessed and Exalted, to let us and you reach it in this year and in those that follow, in goodness and safety, to accept from us and from you, for He is capable of all things.

The plural of majesty comes in regard to His attributes, and the singular comes in regard to His oneness.

From this we know that what is widespread among the common people, that the Night of Decree is the night of the middle of Sha'ban, has no basis and no reality, since the Night of Decree is in Ramadan.

The night of the middle of Sha'ban is like the night of the middle of Rajab, Jumada, Rabi', Safar, Muharram, and other months. It is not specific to anything. As for what has been narrated concerning the virtue of standing in prayer on that night, these are weak hadiths that cannot establish proof. Likewise, what has been narrated concerning singling out its day, which is the fifteenth of Sha'ban, for fasting, these are weak hadiths that cannot establish proof. However, some scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, are lenient in mentioning weak hadiths concerning virtues, whether the virtues of deeds, months, or places. This is not appropriate, because when you narrate weak hadiths about the virtue of anything, the listener will believe it to be authentic and attribute it to the Messenger, peace be upon him, and this is a serious matter. The important point is that the day of the middle of Sha'ban and the night of the middle of Sha'ban are not specific to anything over the rest of the months. The night of the middle is not specific to a virtue of standing in prayer, the night of the middle is not the Night of Decree, and the day of the middle is not specific to fasting.

Yes, regarding the month of Sha'ban, the Sunnah has established that the Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, would fast much during it, so that he broke his fast in it only rarely. Among the scholars are those who said this, and those who said that. The correct view is that it encompasses both meanings. The Night of Decree is without doubt of great standing and great honour, and in it is determined what will occur in that year of giving life and causing death, of provisions, and other matters.
